title: Formal binary Morse normalization with invertible polar matrix
statement: Let $F$ be a field, $S=F[[u,v]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series] and $\mathfrak p=(u,v)$. Let $f\in\mathfrak p^2$ have homogeneous degree-two part $Q=au^2+buv+cv^2$, where $a,b,c\in F$ and $b^2-4ac\ne0$. Then there exists a continuous $F$-algebra automorphism $\alpha:S\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ with $\alpha(u)-u,\alpha(v)-v\in\mathfrak p^2$ and $\alpha(f)=Q$. Continuity is for the $\mathfrak p$-adic topology (the powers $\mathfrak p^N$ form a basis of neighbourhoods of zero). No restriction on the characteristic of $F$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0C49 (lemma-nodal-algebraic), proof of (2) implies (3), successive corrections using the invertible polar matrix; the same correction calculation applied to a single power series before passing to its quotient.

proof.text: Write $f=Q+\sum_{d\ge3}H_d$, where each $H_d$ is homogeneous of degree $d$. The polar linear forms of $Q$ are $L_1=2au+bv$ and $L_2=bu+2cv$; their coefficient matrix has determinant $4ac-b^2\ne0$, so they form a basis of the degree-one forms. Thus $E_2:=f-Q\in\mathfrak p^3$, and we start with $x_2=u$, $y_2=v$ and $f=Q(x_2,y_2)+E_2$.

source.place: Tag 0C49, proof of lemma-nodal-algebraic, setup of the quadratic part and its polar matrix.

proof.text: For each $r\ge2$, the invertibility of the $L_1,L_2$ coefficient matrix means that every homogeneous form of degree $r+1$ can be written $L_1A_r+L_2B_r$ with $A_r,B_r$ homogeneous of degree $r$: this is obtained by expressing one degree-one factor in the basis $L_1,L_2$ and collecting the remaining degree-$r$ factor. This is the only finite-dimensional correction fact used below.

source.place: Tag 0C49, proof of lemma-nodal-algebraic, discussion that the two polar forms are a basis and the successive-correction calculation.

proof.text: Assume inductively that $x_r-u,y_r-v\in\mathfrak p^2$ and that the fixed series $f$ satisfies $f=Q(x_r,y_r)+E_r$ with $E_r\in\mathfrak p^{r+1}$. Let $H_{r+1}$ be the homogeneous degree-$(r+1)$ part of $E_r$, so $E_r-H_{r+1}\in\mathfrak p^{r+2}$. By the preceding basis calculation choose homogeneous $A_r,B_r$ of degree $r$ with $H_{r+1}=L_1A_r+L_2B_r$, and define $x_{r+1}=x_r+A_r(x_r,y_r)$ and $y_{r+1}=y_r+B_r(x_r,y_r)$. For any $x,y,A,B\in S$ one has the exact identity $Q(x+A,y+B)=Q(x,y)+L_1(x,y)A+L_2(x,y)B+Q(A,B)$, by expanding $a(x+A)^2+b(x+A)(y+B)+c(y+B)^2$. Since $x_r\equiv u$, $y_r\equiv v$ modulo $\mathfrak p^2$ and $A_r,B_r$ are homogeneous of degree $r$, we have $A_r(x_r,y_r)-A_r(u,v),B_r(x_r,y_r)-B_r(u,v)\in\mathfrak p^{r+1}$ and $L_i(x_r,y_r)-L_i(u,v)\in\mathfrak p^2$; in particular $A_r(x_r,y_r),B_r(x_r,y_r)\in\mathfrak p^r$. Hence $L_1(x_r,y_r)A_r(x_r,y_r)+L_2(x_r,y_r)B_r(x_r,y_r)\equiv L_1A_r+L_2B_r=H_{r+1}\pmod{\mathfrak p^{r+2}}$, and $Q(A_r(x_r,y_r),B_r(x_r,y_r))\in\mathfrak p^{2r}\subseteq\mathfrak p^{r+2}$ because $r\ge2$. Therefore $Q(x_{r+1},y_{r+1})\equiv Q(x_r,y_r)+H_{r+1}\pmod{\mathfrak p^{r+2}}$, and $E_{r+1}:=f-Q(x_{r+1},y_{r+1})\equiv E_r-H_{r+1}\equiv0\pmod{\mathfrak p^{r+2}}$. The correction lies in $\mathfrak p^r\subseteq\mathfrak p^2$, so $x_{r+1}-u,y_{r+1}-v\in\mathfrak p^2$, completing the induction from the base case of step 1.

source.place: Tag 0C49, proof of lemma-nodal-algebraic, successive corrections: change generators by elements of increasing order and raise the order of vanishing.

proof.text: The increments $x_{r+1}-x_r,\,y_{r+1}-y_r$ lie in $\mathfrak p^r$ for $r\ge2$ (step 3), and $\mathfrak p^r$ consists of the series with no monomial of degree $<r$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Hence for every degree $d$ the coefficients of degree $d$ of $x_r,y_r$ are constant for $r>d$; let $x_\infty,y_\infty\in S$ be the coefficientwise limits. Then $x_\infty-x_r,\,y_\infty-y_r\in\mathfrak p^r$ for every $r\ge2$, and $x_\infty-u,\,y_\infty-v\in\mathfrak p^2$. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-field-cohen-regular-complete] (1) and (4) with $\Lambda=F$, $d=2$, $S$ is a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak p$ and Krull dimension $2$. The classes of $x_\infty,y_\infty$ in $\mathfrak p/\mathfrak p^2$ equal those of $u,v$, which span it; so by [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators], applied to the finitely generated $S$-module $\mathfrak p$, $(x_\infty,y_\infty)=\mathfrak p$. Thus $(x_\infty,y_\infty)$ is a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. By [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-full-coordinates-field] there is an $F$-algebra isomorphism $F[[Y_1,Y_2]]\to S$ with $Y_1\mapsto x_\infty$, $Y_2\mapsto y_\infty$; precomposing with the renaming $S\to F[[Y_1,Y_2]]$, $u\mapsto Y_1$, $v\mapsto Y_2$, gives an $F$-algebra automorphism $\beta$ of $S$ with $\beta(u)=x_\infty$, $\beta(v)=y_\infty$. Since $\beta(\mathfrak p)=(x_\infty,y_\infty)=\mathfrak p$, we get $\beta(\mathfrak p^N)=\mathfrak p^N=\beta^{-1}(\mathfrak p^N)$ for all $N$, so $\beta$ and $\beta^{-1}$ are continuous for the $\mathfrak p$-adic topology. As $Q$ is a polynomial and $\beta$ an $F$-algebra map, $\beta(Q)=Q(x_\infty,y_\infty)$.

source.place: Tag 0C49, proof of lemma-nodal-algebraic, completeness passage from successive corrections to limiting coordinates.

proof.text: For every $r\ge2$, write $x_r=x_\infty+A$, $y_r=y_\infty+B$ with $A,B\in\mathfrak p^r$ (step 4). The identity of step 3 gives $Q(x_r,y_r)-Q(x_\infty,y_\infty)=L_1(x_\infty,y_\infty)A+L_2(x_\infty,y_\infty)B+Q(A,B)\in\mathfrak p^{r+1}$, so $f-\beta(Q)=E_r+\big(Q(x_r,y_r)-Q(x_\infty,y_\infty)\big)\in\mathfrak p^{r+1}$. A series in every $\mathfrak p^{r+1}$ has all coefficients zero [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], hence $f=\beta(Q)$. Let $\alpha=\beta^{-1}$: an $F$-algebra automorphism, continuous by step 4, with $\alpha(\mathfrak p^2)=\mathfrak p^2$. Applying $\alpha$ to $\beta(u)-u\in\mathfrak p^2$ gives $u-\alpha(u)\in\mathfrak p^2$, and likewise $v-\alpha(v)\in\mathfrak p^2$. Applying $\alpha$ to $f=\beta(Q)$ yields $\alpha(f)=Q$. No division by $2$ occurred, so this holds in every characteristic.

The induction now keeps f fixed as f=Q(x_r,y_r)+E_r, chooses positive corrections whose polar contribution cancels the leading class of E_r, and defines the final automorphism as the inverse of the limiting substitution. The elementary homogeneous-basis observation is folded into a proof step, so the spurious homogeneous-correction node is removed.
